newsitem.title: INDIA: Calcutta bourse prices end lower on low volumes.
newsitem.headline: Calcutta bourse prices end lower on low volumes.

text.p: Calcutta shares closed lower on Monday amidst low volumes and lack of buying interest from retailers and foreign funds, brokers said.
They said that most blue-chips that opened weak, failed to recover as none of the big players in the secondary market placed any significant buy orders.

"There seems to be crisis of confidence among all large investors. It is not that there has been an increase in selling by the foreign funds but their purchases have surely come down drastically," said Aprajit Sharma of brokers Jet Age Securities.

"The downward movement of stock prices is a reaction to disappointment over the Indian finance minister's measures for the capital markets. Market technicals once again definitely looks bearish and a recovery seems very distant," Sharma said.
